othello: Shakespeare's source took months. Why squeeze it into two days?
Othello's last speech: noble at last, or hiding from what he did?
Iago gives at least four motives. Why does none of them add up?
Each woman in Othello is branded unchaste. Who gets to say so?
Was Othello written to question racism, or does it repeat it?
Othello says he 'loved not wisely, but too well'. Is that true?
Each age has made a different Othello. Whose reading is right?
king-lear: Why does King Lear tell the same story twice?
Does Lear learn anything, or does he just suffer?
Is Edmund a born villain, or made one by his world?
Are Goneril and Regan monsters, or daughters with a point?
Lear and Edmund both pray to Nature. Do they mean the same thing?
Gloucester only sees the truth once he's blind. How can that be?
After all that suffering, is there any comfort in King Lear?
hamlet: Revenge plays had a recipe. Does Hamlet follow it or rewrite it?
Hamlet says he'll fake madness. Does he stay in control of it?
Claudius kneels to pray for forgiveness. Is he a monster?
Polonius's family mirrors Hamlet's. What does the mirror show?
A Wittenberg student meets a ghost from purgatory. Trust it?
Something is rotten in the state of Denmark. Where does it start?
Every age finds its own Hamlet. So which reading is right?
tess-of-the-durbervilles: Hardy cuts Tess's life into seven 'Phases'. Why not just chapters?
Does Tess act, or is she only acted upon?
Alec ruins Tess. Angel abandons her. Which man harms her more?
Is Tess destroyed by fate, by chance, or by other people?
Tess thrives at one farm, suffers at another. Why does place matter?
Hardy's subtitle calls Tess 'A Pure Woman'. Why did that shock?
Hardy's narrator defends Tess and stares at her. Can it do both?
frankenstein: Three narrators, one monster. Whose story can we trust?
Prometheus stole fire for humanity. What did Victor steal?
The monster speaks better than his maker. Why give him the best lines?
The women barely speak. Is that the novel's flaw or its point?
Shelley rewrote Frankenstein in 1831. Did science become the villain?
Mountains heal Victor, ice kills him. What is nature doing?
Feminist, Freudian, Marxist: can one monster mean all three?
dracula: Journals, letters, cuttings: why does Dracula never get a diary?
Why does a vampire spend his evenings reading train timetables?
Five men, one vampire. Why do the heroes need so many?
Mina mocks the New Woman. So why does she do the men's work?
Harker is terrified of the vampire women. So why does he wait?
Typewriters, phonographs, transfusions. Can 1890s science beat him?
One vampire, five critics. Which reading is the right one?
wuthering-heights: Why do a stranger and a servant tell this great love story?
Heathcliff opens Catherine's coffin. Why do readers still pity him?
Catherine says “I am Heathcliff.” So why marry Edgar?
The story ends with a reading lesson. Is that a happy ending?
A ghost at the window, an opened grave: is this a Gothic novel?
Heathcliff never kills anyone. So how does he take two houses?
Same novel, three critics, three different books. Who's right?
